summary_html: The **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** created a national commission to study child-fatality prevention. Project Milk Carton cross-references its findings with state fatality data to expose non-implementation. In Alabama the age of majority is 19 (Ala. Code § 26-1-1), and for child abuse and neglect reporting a "child" is a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services (Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3)).
authority_html: - **Public Law 112-275 (Protect Our Kids Act)** — national commission and reporting framework

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court denied State-agent immunity to the CA/N investigator, who never made the home visit required by Ala. Admin. Code r. 660-5-34-.05(1)(b), and to the ongoing worker, who ignored her supervisor's binding written instructions, but granted immunity to the two supervisors whose duties involved judgment.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion is a detailed judicial post-mortem of the agency failures preceding a child fatality.
key_cases.quote: because Watson has not submitted substantial evidence indicating that she complied with subsection (b), Watson has not demonstrated that she is entitled to State-agent immunity

key_cases.case_name: Brakefield v. Alabama Department of Human Resources
key_cases.holding: The Court declined to overrule Mitchell v. Davis and held that foster parents are protected by parental immunity from simple-negligence claims by a foster child, so the negligence claims arising from the child's drowning were barred, while the wantonness claims could proceed.
key_cases.relevance: The case illustrates the accountability gap that fatality review is meant to fill, since negligence claims are immunized.
key_cases.quote: negligence claims against the Spurgeons are barred by the doctrine of parental immunity

key_cases.case_name: R.C. ex rel. Alabama Disabilities Advocacy Program v. Walley
key_cases.court: United States District Court for the Middle District of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court granted the Commissioner's second motion to terminate the 1991 R.C. consent decree, finding that DHR had met both prongs of the termination clause by achieving and being able to sustain systemwide substantial compliance so that continued judicial oversight was no longer necessary.
key_cases.relevance: The decree's system-of-care standards were adopted after conditions the court called depraved, including harm to children in care.
key_cases.quote: DHR successfully has reformed its child welfare system by developing a system of care which substantially complies with the requirements of the Consent Decree and the Implementation Plan
